-- =============================================================
-- 11_detection_quality.sql
-- How good is the z-score detector (04_anomaly_detection.sql)?
--
-- The synthetic generator labels every fault it injects (is_anomaly):
-- either a zero-value dropout or a spike at 3x the sensor's normal
-- maximum. As in 04_anomaly_detection.sql, the labels are used only to
-- build a clean baseline (monthly mean and standard deviation of the
-- non-injected readings); the flag itself is z > 3 on the value alone.
-- Comparing flags with labels gives precision and recall per sensor
-- type and fault kind.
--
-- Typical result: precision is 100% and every spike is caught, but a
-- zero reading is only caught when zero lies far outside the sensor's
-- normal range (bus voltage). For power, temperature, irradiance and
-- wind speed, zero is an ordinary value, so a dropout there is
-- statistically invisible and needs a different rule.
--
-- Techniques: CTEs, aggregate FILTER clauses, boolean expressions
-- Served by: GET /api/detection-quality
-- =============================================================

WITH sensor_monthly_stats AS (
    SELECT
        sensor_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', recorded_at)  AS month,
        AVG(value)                        AS mean_val,
        STDDEV(value)                     AS stddev_val
    FROM readings
    WHERE is_anomaly = FALSE
    GROUP BY sensor_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', recorded_at)
),
scored AS (
    SELECT
        se.sensor_type,
        r.is_anomaly                                         AS injected,
        (s.stddev_val > 0
         AND ABS(r.value - s.mean_val) / s.stddev_val > 3)   AS flagged,
        r.value < s.mean_val                                 AS below_baseline
    FROM readings r
    JOIN sensor_monthly_stats s
      ON  r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
      AND DATE_TRUNC('month', r.recorded_at) = s.month
    JOIN sensors se ON r.sensor_id = se.sensor_id
)
SELECT
    sensor_type,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected)                                  AS injected,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE flagged)                                   AS flagged,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND flagged)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE flagged), 0), 1)            AS precision_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND flagged)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected), 0), 1)           AS recall_pct,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND NOT below_baseline AND flagged) || ' / ' ||
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND NOT below_baseline)           AS spikes_caught,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND below_baseline AND flagged)   || ' / ' ||
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected AND below_baseline)               AS drops_caught
FROM scored
GROUP BY sensor_type
ORDER BY sensor_type;

-- =============================================================
-- 12_zero_dropout_rules.sql
-- Can a rule other than z > 3 catch zero-value dropouts?
--
-- The z-score detector (11_detection_quality.sql) misses every injected
-- zero on sensors whose normal range contains zero (power, temperature,
-- wind speed, irradiance). This query scores three alternative rules
-- against the injected zeros (is_anomaly AND value = 0):
--
--   flatline_3       value is 0 and the two previous readings were 0 too
--                    (a "stuck sensor" rule, common on real equipment)
--   neighbour_drop   value is below 5 % of the smaller neighbouring reading
--   exact_zero       value is exactly 0
--
-- Why the results look the way they do: the generator injects faults as
-- isolated single readings (a random 2 % mask), and draws normal values
-- uniformly at random. So a stuck-sensor rule finds almost nothing, the
-- neighbour rule fires on any naturally low value, and exact_zero is perfect
-- only because clean synthetic readings are never exactly 0.0, which would
-- not hold for real telemetry.
--
-- The labels (is_anomaly) are used only for scoring, never by the rules.
-- Techniques: LAG/LEAD window functions, named WINDOW, FILTER aggregates
-- =============================================================

WITH neighbours AS (
    SELECT
        se.sensor_type,
        r.value,
        r.is_anomaly AND r.value = 0                 AS injected_zero,
        LAG(r.value, 1)  OVER w                      AS prev_1,
        LAG(r.value, 2)  OVER w                      AS prev_2,
        LEAD(r.value, 1) OVER w                      AS next_1
    FROM readings r
    JOIN sensors se ON se.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY r.sensor_id ORDER BY r.recorded_at)
),
rules AS (
    SELECT sensor_type, injected_zero, 'flatline_3' AS rule,
           (value = 0 AND prev_1 = 0 AND prev_2 = 0) AS flagged
    FROM neighbours
    UNION ALL
    SELECT sensor_type, injected_zero, 'neighbour_drop',
           COALESCE(value < 0.05 * LEAST(prev_1, next_1), FALSE)
    FROM neighbours
    UNION ALL
    SELECT sensor_type, injected_zero, 'exact_zero', value = 0
    FROM neighbours
)
SELECT
    rule,
    sensor_type,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected_zero)                         AS injected_zeros,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected_zero AND flagged)             AS caught,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE flagged)                               AS flagged,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected_zero AND flagged)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected_zero), 0), 1)  AS recall_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injected_zero AND flagged)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE flagged), 0), 1)        AS precision_pct
FROM rules
GROUP BY rule, sensor_type
ORDER BY rule, sensor_type;

-- =============================================================
-- 08_real_vs_synthetic_comparison.sql
-- Compares real Fingrid wind production data against the
-- synthetic generated wind readings on a daily scale.
-- Applies z-score standardization to normalize both series:
-- (value - AVG(value) OVER ()) / STDDEV(value) OVER ()
-- Computes the Pearson correlation coefficient using CORR().
-- =============================================================

WITH real_daily AS (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', recorded_at) AS day, 
           AVG(value) AS real_avg
    FROM grid_data
    WHERE metric = 'wind_production'
    GROUP BY 1
),
synthetic_daily AS (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', r.recorded_at) AS day, 
           AVG(r.value) AS synthetic_avg
    FROM readings r
    JOIN sensors s ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
    JOIN facilities f ON s.facility_id = f.facility_id
    WHERE f.facility_type = 'wind' AND s.sensor_type = 'power_output'
    GROUP BY 1
),
daily_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        r.day,
        r.real_avg,
        s.synthetic_avg,
        (r.real_avg - AVG(r.real_avg) OVER ()) / NULLIF(STDDEV(r.real_avg) OVER (), 0) AS real_z,
        (s.synthetic_avg - AVG(s.synthetic_avg) OVER ()) / NULLIF(STDDEV(s.synthetic_avg) OVER (), 0) AS synthetic_z
    FROM real_daily r
    JOIN synthetic_daily s ON r.day = s.day
)
SELECT 
    TO_CHAR(day, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS day_label,
    ROUND(real_avg::numeric, 4) AS real_avg,
    ROUND(synthetic_avg::numeric, 4) AS synthetic_avg,
    ROUND(real_z::numeric, 4) AS real_z,
    ROUND(synthetic_z::numeric, 4) AS synthetic_z,
    ROUND(CORR(synthetic_z, real_z) OVER ()::numeric, 4) AS correlation_coefficient
FROM daily_metrics
ORDER BY day;
